body:
TVS Capital Funds (TCF) has entered India's private credit market with the launch of TVS Alts, targeting an initial fund corpus of Rs 750 crore and a green-shoe option of Rs 500 crore. The platform plans to provide secured financing to performing mid-market companies, with individual investments ranging from Rs 40 crore to Rs 100 crore.

The move marks TCF's expansion beyond its established private equity business into alternative lending, as it looks to finance companies with sound credit profiles and strong underlying fundamentals. The proposed fund will focus on opportunities across sectors, including bridge financing, pre-initial public offering (IPO) funding and mergers and acquisitions (M&A)-related financing.

TVS Alts will follow a sector-agnostic investment strategy, focusing on companies with sound credit profiles, adequate security and strong business fundamentals. The fund is targeting returns of around 16 to 17 per cent from its lending portfolio.

The proposed financing will cater to businesses seeking capital for short-term liquidity requirements, pre-IPO funding and acquisition-related transactions. The fund has already evaluated 42 potential investment opportunities, of which two or three are under consideration. Active deal origination is expected to begin after the platform receives the necessary regulatory approvals.

Regulatory Approvals And Fundraising Timeline

TVS Alts has received internal approvals and filed applications with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi). The company expects to receive the requisite regulatory clearances in the coming weeks.

The platform aims to complete its first close within six months of receiving regulatory approval and achieve its final close within 12 to 14 months. The initial fund is expected to make approximately 14 to 15 investments over its lifetime.

The fundraising strategy will rely predominantly on domestic capital, with potential investors including insurance companies, bank treasuries and corporates seeking to diversify their investment portfolios.

Leadership And Ownership Structure

Shyam Srinivasan, Executive Chairman of TVS Alternatives and Senior Advisor and Operating Partner at TVS Capital Funds, is among the founders of the new platform and will lead its development.

Manish Makaria, who previously worked with TVS Capital Funds and subsequently with SBI Funds Management, will serve as Managing Partner. The platform's leadership team brings experience across commercial banking, private equity, investment banking and recovery.

The board will include Prasad Gopalan, a former senior executive at the International Finance Corporation; banking veteran Ashutosh Khajuria; former SIDBI executive Mani Krishna Iyer; and industrialist Srilalitha Gopal. TVS Capital Funds holds a 90 per cent stake in TVS Alts, while Shyam Srinivasan owns the remaining 10 per cent.

Expansion Beyond Private Equity

Founded in 2007 by Gopal Srinivasan, TVS Capital Funds has focused on growth-stage investments in Indian businesses. The private credit entry expands its investment activities into an additional financial services segment.

The launch follows the firm's recent closure of its fourth private equity fund, which has a corpus of nearly Rs 4,000 crore. The company is also looking at opportunities across other financial services verticals, including wealth management and asset management, over the longer term. TVS Capital is considering raising additional private credit funds over the next three to five years as the strategy develops.
